$meta.name: Portfolio Design System
$meta.colorSpace: OKLCH (CSS Color Module 4), sRGB hex fallback provided for every value
$meta.contrastStandard: WCAG 2.2 - relative luminance contrast per §1.4.3 (text, 4.5:1 / 3:1 large) and §1.4.11 (non-text UI components, 3:1)
$meta.structure: primitives = raw color scales (source of truth). tokens = semantic layer; every token's `ref` points back into primitives.
$meta.usageNote: Fetch this file and read tokens.* directly for component styling. primitives.* exists for building new tokens or design tooling (Figma variables, Style Dictionary, Tailwind config) - do not hardcode primitive values directly into components.

neutral.role: UI neutral gray (subtle warm undertone, independent of Secondary)

violet.role: Semantic - links (shares hue family with Accent 2)

default.usage: Primary page background.

subtle.usage: Alternating section background / zebra striping on the page canvas.

muted.usage: Tertiary tint for large decorative sections; avoid placing body text directly on this without re-checking contrast.

default.usage: Card, panel, and container background sitting above the canvas.

sunken.usage: Inset wells: code blocks, quote blocks, input containers at rest.

default.usage: Dark sections: nav bar, hero, footer. This is the exact Secondary brand color.

subtle.usage: Secondary dark surface stacked on top of inverse.default (e.g. a card inside a dark footer).

muted.usage: Tertiary dark surface / hover state for inverse.subtle.

default.usage: Brand-colored section band or CTA banner. This is the exact Primary brand hex.

contrast.cream.50 (page): 1.35:1 vs cream.50 [FAIL - do not use for text or required UI boundaries]

default.notes: Low luminance-contrast against canvas (1.35:1) — an isolated gold block on cream needs a border, shadow, or generous whitespace gap to read as a distinct region.

subtle.usage: Soft brand-tinted highlight box (e.g. a callout or quote background).

default.usage: Large decorative color block using the exact Accent-1 brand hex. Pair only with ink.950 foreground content, never white.

contrast.cream.50 (page): 2.60:1 vs cream.50 [FAIL - do not use for text or required UI boundaries]

default.usage: Decorative color block using the exact Accent-2 brand hex.

scrim.usage: Modal / drawer backdrop scrim placed over page content.

disabled.usage: Background for disabled containers (e.g. a disabled card or input wrapper).

background.usage: Base elevation for cards and static panels.

border.usage: Decorative separation from canvas; not a required 3:1 boundary since the card shape/shadow is not solely color-dependent.

background.ref: literal white (brighter than neutral.50 by design, for pop-over emphasis)
background.usage: Dropdowns, modals, popovers — content that floats above layer 1.
Tooltips and toasts intentionally break the light elevation pattern and float as dark chips for maximum visual priority.
Inset wells sitting below the surrounding surface: code blocks, quote blocks.

primary.usage: Default body copy, headings — the highest-emphasis text color on light surfaces.

secondary.usage: Supporting copy, sub-headings, captions with real informational content.
secondary.notes: This is the minimum ink step that clears 4.5:1 body-text AA on cream.50. Do not go lighter (ink.600 and up only clear the 3:1 large-text/UI tier).

tertiary.usage: Large-scale (≥18.66px bold / ≥24px regular) supporting text, or non-essential microcopy where 3:1 is sufficient.

contrast.cream.50: 3.25:1 vs cream.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

tertiary.notes: FAILS AA for body-sized text. Restrict to large text or decorative use only.

contrast.cream.50: 1.79:1 vs cream.50 [FAIL - do not use for text or required UI boundaries]

disabled.notes: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled content from contrast minimums. Ratio shown for reference only — do not use this token for anything but genuinely disabled state.

contrast.neutral.50 (field bg): 3.22:1 vs neutral.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

placeholder.notes: Placeholder text is not classified as WCAG 'text' and is exempt from 4.5:1, but never use a placeholder as the only label for a field (WCAG 3.3.2) — always pair with a persistent visible label using text.secondary or darker.

default.usage: Inline brand-colored text/emphasis on light surfaces (minimum accessible step).

strong.usage: Higher-contrast brand text where AAA is desired.

accent.usage: Inline Accent-1-colored text on light surfaces.
accent.notes: orange.500 (the literal brand hex) is a fill color only — never use it as text color on light surfaces.

disabled.usage: Disabled text on dark surfaces (exempt from minimums).

contrast.ink.950: 3.37:1 vs ink.950 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

subtle.usage: Decorative dividers/edges not required to identify a component (exempt from 3:1).

default.usage: Resting-state boundary for interactive components (inputs, outlined buttons, checkboxes, cards that are clickable).

contrast.cream.50: 3.22:1 vs cream.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

default.notes: This is the minimum neutral step clearing WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text contrast requirement against the cream canvas.

hover.usage: Hover-state boundary, one step stronger than default.

strong.usage: High-emphasis boundary (e.g. a selected card, an important container).

focus.usage: Focus-visible outline/ring color, brand-consistent and WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11-compliant.

subtle.usage: Decorative divider on dark surfaces (exempt from 3:1).

default.usage: Interactive component boundary on dark (ink.950) surfaces.

contrast.ink.950: 3.37:1 vs ink.950 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

default.notes: Minimum neutral step clearing 3:1 against ink.950.

default.usage: Resting input background.
Resting input border.

contrast.neutral.50: 3.22:1 vs neutral.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

focus.usage: Focus-state input border, paired with a soft outer glow (gold.300 @ 30% alpha).

label.usage: Field label, always visible (never substitute with placeholder alone).

default.usage: Field-adjacent icon (e.g. search, calendar).
Default link color on light surfaces.

visited.usage: Visited-link color, deliberately deeper/duller than default.

focus.usage: Focus-visible ring around a focused link, matching border.focus.

default.usage: Default link color on dark (ink.950) surfaces — this is the exact Accent-2 brand hex, repurposed functionally.

hover.usage: Hover-state link on dark surfaces (lighter = higher emphasis on dark backgrounds).

underline.usage: Optional decorative underline color when a subtler rule than the link text itself is wanted (decorative, exempt from 3:1).

default.usage: Default icon color on light surfaces — deliberately a touch stronger than text.secondary since icons read best at high clarity.

contrast.cream.50: 3.25:1 vs cream.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

subtle.notes: Only meets the 3:1 large-graphic tier — do not use for icons that are the sole carrier of meaning.

default.usage: Icon color on dark surfaces.

accent.notes: orange.500 is a fill color only; use orange.700 whenever the orange itself must serve as the meaningful foreground shape.

default.usage: Primary CTA fill — the exact Primary brand hex.

contrast.cream.50 (page): 1.35:1 vs cream.50 [FAIL - do not use for text or required UI boundaries]

default.usage: Label text on the gold fill.

required.notes: Gold fills sit at only 1.35-2.35:1 luminance-contrast against the cream.50 canvas at every step (300-500), failing WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text requirement. A solid ink.950 (or neutral.800) border is required so the button boundary remains perceivable without relying on hue alone.

default.usage: Secondary button fill — the exact Secondary brand hex.
Label text.

focusRing.usage: 2px offset focus-visible ring, doubles as brand accent.

contrast.ink.950 (button): 3.34:1 vs ink.950 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

default.usage: Label text.
Resting outline.

contrast.cream.50: 3.22:1 vs cream.50 [AA (large text / UI components only)]

default.usage: Destructive action fill.
Label text.
Accent CTA fill — deliberately deeper than the raw Accent-1 brand hex so white label text stays AA-compliant.
Label text.

accent.notes: orange.500 (FF702E, the exact brand Accent-1 hex) fails with both white text (2.76:1) and is marginal with ink.950 text (6.04:1, workable but inconsistent across hover/active steps). This button uses orange.700 as its base so the full default/hover/active ladder can share one consistent white label color.

subtle.usage: Success chip/badge text on soft fill.

solid.usage: Success chip/badge text on solid fill.

subtle.usage: Error chip/badge text on soft fill.

solid.usage: Error chip/badge text on solid fill.

subtle.usage: Alert chip/badge text on soft fill.

solid.usage: Alert chip/badge text on solid fill.

subtle.usage: Info chip/badge text on soft fill.

solid.usage: Info chip/badge text on solid fill.

subtle.usage: Neutral chip/badge text on soft fill.

solid.usage: Neutral chip/badge text on solid fill.

default.usage: Inactive tab label.

active.notes: Meets the 3:1 non-text requirement for state indicators; gold.300/400/500 do not and should not be used here.

default.usage: Standard divider on light surfaces (decorative, exempt from 3:1).

strong.usage: Higher-emphasis section divider on light surfaces.

brand.usage: Decorative brand-tinted divider (e.g. under a section heading).
